questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Tunisia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Tunisia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Tunisia article.

questions.proof: It shares its borders with two countries including Algeria to the west, and Libya to the southeast.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Tunisia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Demographics” part of the Tunisia article.

questions.proof: Standard Arabic is the official language by the Tunisian constitution.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Tunisia became officially a French protectorate in on May 12, 1881, but with the strong opposition of the kingdom of _____ because there was a huge Italian community in Tunisia.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “kingdom”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “French Occupation” part of the Tunisia article.

questions.proof: Tunisia became officially a French protectorate in on May 12, 1881, but with the strong opposition of the kingdom of Italy because there was a huge Italian community in Tunisia.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Important parts of the North African Campaign of World War II were fought in Tunisia from _____ to 1943.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “World War II” part of the Tunisia article.

questions.proof: Important parts of the North African Campaign of World War II were fought in Tunisia from 1941 to 1943.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Ben Ali ruled as dictator of the country until _____, when he was overthrown in a revolution.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Independence and revolution” part of the Tunisia article.

questions.proof: Ben Ali ruled as dictator of the country until 2011, when he was overthrown in a revolution.
